scores.notes:
Scale: six criteria, each 1-10, total out of 60.
- Clarity of purpose 9: 'spend your attention carefully' is one sentence that explains every screen; Now vs Sky is a clean act/aware split.
- Speed to unblock 9: a ranked stream with Undoable swipes, a batch bar and deep links straight to the card is the fastest path of the three.
- Trust and safety 9: reversibility-shaped cards, confirmed-delivery-only animation and named failure outcomes are excellent; it loses a point for offering 'don't ask again' ('2') remotely when the prompt has it.
- Delight 9: Runway, final-approach arrivals, star twinkle per real tool call and the contracting ring are rich and every effect maps to a signal.
- Coherence across iPhone, Android and Mac 9: the same two destinations, pulse and Runway on all three, plus a real presence hand-off; the Now/Sky horizontal swipe collides with card swipes and must be resolved.
- Room to grow 8: Brief, review lane, runway-aware dispatch and rule suggestions all slot in, but it has no outcome/'shipped' story or day history beyond a log.

Scale: six criteria, each 1-10, total out of 60.
- Clarity of purpose 8: 'what got done, what is blocked, what it cost' is a strong frame, but outcome-first makes the home screen a story when the primary job is unblocking.
- Speed to unblock 7: only two amber cards at the waterline, then a tide pill and a Triage sheet; one extra hop for every approval beyond two.
- Trust and safety 9: the exact delivery preview ('Will type 1 into Terminal tab api-gateway'), staleness guard, receipt-then-cancel window and audit-in-the-story are the best receipts of the three; 'Always allow' writing settings files from a phone tap is a trust shift that needs a user decision.
- Delight 8: sunrise proportional to work done, the light thread to the Mac chip and the Story-to-Fleet morph are memorable; the day scrubber is clever but adds a third control to the rail.
- Coherence 8: the Mac 'Step away' and 'Welcome back' loop is the best hand-off idea; three zoom levels plus a floating layer is more model to learn on Android.
- Room to grow 9: outcome ledger, cost per outcome, wait cost, standups and thread memory give it the longest runway as a product.

Scale: six criteria, each 1-10, total out of 60.
- Clarity of purpose 8: 'lead a crew' is instantly graspable; the teammate abstraction is a layer over pid-keyed sessions that users must trust is right.
- Speed to unblock 8: inline Approve/Deny on the roster and swipe-up-for-next-ask on the Ask card are fast; risk-flagged slide-to-approve is a good brake.
- Trust and safety 9: the locked composer while waiting, never sending '2', and pid-liveness plus screen-fingerprint before every injection are exactly right for Claude Code's keystroke semantics; anthropomorphism ('moods', 'teammates') nudges people to trust faster.
- Delight 7: breathing avatar rings and dusk/dawn battery pauses are lovely, but the roster is still a styled list and the metaphor risks feeling cute.
- Coherence 8: Crew Board popover and an optional full Crew window give the Mac a real role; foldable list-detail on Android is a good touch.
- Room to grow 8: standing handoffs, standup planner and capacity planning are strong, but everything depends on a synthetic cwd+kind registry that can mis-merge worktrees and parallel sessions.

direction:
PAGE v4 · NIGHT WATCH. Base: Calm Dispatch. Grafts: Handover's receipts, delivery preview, return story and day log; The Crew's keystroke discipline (locked composer, never '2', pid plus screen-fingerprint check) and its stable per-project identity.

THESIS: Page keeps watch over your agents so you don't have to. It does three things, in this order.
1. KEEP THEM RUNNING: the Mac stays awake, agents pause gracefully at the cutoff, and the usage window is forecast. All three show on one Runway at the top of every screen.
2. UNBLOCK THEM SAFELY: one ranked stream of what needs you. Every card is shaped by how reversible its action is, and every action names the exact keystroke and terminal it will reach.
3. TELL YOU THE TRUTH: success animates only after the Mac confirms the keystroke landed. Silence ('All quiet') is earned and accurate. Coming back gives you one honest story of your absence instead of N logs.

NAVIGATION: two places and one verb.
- NOW is where you act: the ranked stream, the brief, and the log as you scroll.
- SKY is where you're aware: the fleet as constellations, with a Lanes list for accessibility and density.
- THE PULSE starts work, and held down it stops everything.
- Settings and power share one sheet, the Tower, opened from the Mac chip or the Runway.
- A session is never a destination. It is a room you zoom into from the card or star that brought you there.

DESIGN WORLD: night sky; one living pulse (teal = working, amber = needs you, still = quiet); aurora intensity = fleet activity; liquid-glass surfaces; red reserved for two press-and-hold commits only. Every animation is a state change, a direction of travel or a receipt, never decoration.

BUILDABILITY: everything on the first-glance screen comes from data Page already has: sessions/<pid>.json status, transcripts and TurnDigest/TurnSummary, stuck heuristics, rate limits, BatteryForecast, UsageForecast, ResumeScheduler, UserPresence, delivery results and the page/reply log. The only new components v4.0 needs are:
- (a) a conservative Mac-side reversibility classifier;
- (b) a Live Activity and an Android live-update notification;
- (c) the Return Brief aggregator over the existing log;
- (d) a stable star avatar seeded from a hash of the cwd (no registry);
- (e) a per-session state-transition log on the Mac. sessions/<pid>.json only holds the current status, so this log records busy/waiting/idle/stuck/rate-limited/paused transitions, each with a timestamp, plus which device answered each page. It feeds the Lanes activity strip and the Brief's 'from iPhone / at the Mac' split.

Loading earlier sessions from the same folder into a Session Room's Story is new relay protocol work, Claude transcripts only, and is scheduled for v4.1.
navigation:
WHAT HAPPENS TO THE OLD TABS
- Inbox and Sessions-as-a-list merge into NOW.
- History becomes SETTLED, which you reach by scrolling past the live items in Now. Lines are grouped by day, and each past day collapses to a headline card ('Tue · 14 decided · 6 finished · 2 stuck · battery pause ×1').
- Settings becomes the TOWER sheet.
- Session detail becomes the SESSION ROOM, a zoom and never a tab.

TOP-LEVEL DESTINATIONS (exactly two)
1. NOW, the ranked stream. It is the default on launch and the target of every deep link.
2. SKY, the fleet. Its modes are Sky (constellations) and Lanes (an accessible, sortable list with a 4-hour activity strip per row). The last mode used is remembered.

ONE VERB: THE PULSE, centred in the nav capsule.
- Tap: open Dispatch.
- Press and hold: the Stop ring. The ring appears only after 300 ms, so a slow tap never starts it. It then fills over 1.5 s with haptic ticks, and completing it asks for Face ID / Touch ID / fingerprint. The confirmation names the scope ('Press Esc in 4 busy sessions'), so a mis-hold costs two deliberate steps.
- Stop is also in the Tower and in Sky long-press, so the hold is a shortcut, not the only path.

SHEETS AND ROOMS (never tabs)
- DECISION SHEET: grows from a card.
- SESSION ROOM: zooms from a card, star or lane. Its lenses are Story, Screen, Changes and Workflows.
- DISPATCH: rises from the pulse.
- TOWER: drops from the Mac chip. It holds Power, Budget, Macs, Attention, Standing replies, Agent hooks, and Pairing and encryption. Tapping the Runway opens the Tower scrolled to Budget.

iPHONE
- A floating liquid-glass capsule, 64 pt tall with 16 pt margins: [Now] · (pulse 52 pt) · [Sky]. Each side shows a badge: Now shows the Decide count in amber; Sky shows the working count in teal.
- HORIZONTAL SWIPE has one owner per region:
  - in the Now stream, horizontal swipe belongs to cards (Undoable cards only);
  - switching between Now and Sky is a tap on the capsule, a horizontal drag on the capsule itself, or a horizontal swipe on the Horizon band at the top. The aurora pans as one continuous sky, and Sky lies to the right of Now;
  - the leftmost 20 pt edge is always system back.
- Pull down on the Horizon to re-sync with the Mac. If you were away 10 min or more, pulling past the detent re-opens the last Return Brief.
- Long-press any card or star for Hold (snooze pages from that session for 15 min, 1 h, or 'until I'm at the desk'), Open on Mac, and Stop this session.
- Every notification, Live Activity tap and widget tap deep-links to the exact card's Decision Sheet, with Now underneath, never to a tab.
- Action Button / Control Center: 'Open Now', with the count. It never acts on its own.
- Siri is read-only for anything Contained or above: 'What are my agents doing?' reads the Horizon sentence and the top item.

PAGER SURFACES (where most interactions begin)
- NOTIFICATION:
  - Line 1: the project, plus the kind (Approval / Question / Plan / Stuck / Rate limit / Finished / Forecast).
  - Line 2: the already-redacted one-liner, for example 'wants to run [Bash] swift test'.
  - Trailing: the class chip (Undoable / Contained / Irreversible).
  - Threaded per session, so each session collapses into one thread, never a stack.
  - Actions: Approve / Deny for Undoable items only, behind authentication-required. 'Open to decide' for Contained and Irreversible.
  - File names, commands beyond the redacted line, diffs and transcripts never appear in a notification.
- LIVE ACTIVITY / DYNAMIC ISLAND (new in v4.0):
  - Compact view: the pulse and the Decide count.
  - Minimal view: the pulse.
  - Expanded view: the top Decide item (verb-first title plus class chip), the next Runway marker ('cutoff 01:40' / '5h limit 03:10'), and the working count.
  - It starts when the Mac reports you're away, and ends when you return or when all is quiet for 30 min.
- LOCK SCREEN WIDGETS:
  - Circular: the pulse plus the count.
  - Rectangular: a Runway arc with the next marker.
- HOME WIDGETS:
  - Medium: the top 3 items plus the Runway strip.
  - Large: a mini Sky of constellations with the Horizon sentence.
  - Each widget item deep-links to its card.

ANDROID (Material 3 Expressive, dynamic colour off, night-sky theme)
- The bottom nav is a floating glass pill: Now, a centred pulse FAB, and Sky. The FAB morphs into the Dispatch sheet (container transform).
- The Mac chip sits in the top app bar and opens the Tower as a modal bottom sheet.
- Predictive back shrinks the Session Room or Decision Sheet back into the exact card, star or lane it came from, with a live preview during the gesture.
- Ongoing live-update notification (Android 16 progress-style; new): the pulse state, the Decide count, the top item, and the next Runway marker.
- Notification actions: Approve and Deny appear only for Undoable items, with setAuthenticationRequired. Every item also gets 'Tell it…' (RemoteInput), which Page always delivers as Esc, then the text, then Enter.
- Quick Settings tile: shows the pulse state and opens Now.
- Glance widgets mirror the iOS widgets.
- Foldables and tablets: list-detail, with Now on the left and the Decision Sheet or Session Room on the right. Sky gets a two-pane view: constellations plus Lanes.

MAC (menu bar: ambient by default, dispatcher at the desk)
- The menu-bar glyph is the pulse itself:
  - teal breath while agents work;
  - amber with a count when something is blocked;
  - a hollow ring when keep-awake is off;
  - a tiny moon tick when lid-closed awake is active;
  - a hairline arc around the dot showing battery headroom to the cutoff;
  - a flat horizon line under the dot while agents are paused for battery.
- Click, or press Option-Command-P from anywhere, to open the liquid-glass popover. It is Now in compact form: the Horizon line, the Runway, Decide/Look/Review rows, then the In-flight strip. A 'Now | Sky' segment switches to a compact constellation strip with Lanes.
- Keyboard: Up/Down move between cards. 1 approves; Return approves Undoable items only. Esc denies. T means 'Tell it instead'. O focuses the real Terminal, iTerm2 or cmux pane. Command-N opens Dispatch. Holding Command-period stops all agents.
- The footer has 'Step away', 'Stop my agents' (hold) and Preferences. The Tower's full controls live in Preferences.
- PRESENCE HAND-OFF (UserPresence):
  - At the desk, finished, idle and forecast pages stay on the Mac and the phone is quiet. Approvals and questions still page both devices, resolve on whichever answers first, and the other device shows 'Answered on Mac' / 'Answered on iPhone'.
  - Going idle past the 'away' threshold, or pressing Step away, makes the glyph send one ripple outward and shows a small phone badge (paging armed). The phone's Live Activity starts.
  - On return, a Welcome back panel drops from the menu bar.
firstGlance:
NOW on iPhone, top to bottom, at 01:12 with agents running.

RULE ZERO: if anything is blocked on you, the first card under the Runway is that card. No brief, sunrise or animation ever sits in front of a Decide card.

1. THE HORIZON (top ~24%, safe area included)
- Aurora low on the horizon. The single pulse is centred (56 pt).
- Under the pulse, one dispatcher sentence, built deterministically from events with no model call: '2 need you · 5 working · runway clear till 03:40'. When you've been away 10 min or more, the sentence is phrased as a handover: 'While you were away (1h 52m) · 3 finished · 2 need you'.
- The Mac chip at top-left: 'Studio MBP · lid closed · 41%'. It turns amber when the cutoff is under 30 min. Tap it to open the Tower.
- Pulse states:
  - amber, rippling once per waiting item, with a ripple rate that rises gently with the longest wait, capped at 1 ripple every 1.5 s;
  - teal breathing when only working;
  - still star-white when quiet.
- Why first: it answers 'do I need to do anything, and will my agents keep running?' before you read a word.

2. THE RUNWAY (a 44 pt glass strip covering the next 6 hours)
- A 'now' tick at the left. Markers slide toward 'now' in real time.
- The markers:
  - battery cutoff at the current drain (BatteryForecast), or a full horizon line when on AC;
  - the 5h limit at the current pace, and the 5h reset (UsageForecast);
  - scheduled resumes after rate limits, with their pmset wake (ResumeScheduler);
  - the 7d reset when it falls inside the window.
- A marker turns amber when it is predicted to land before in-flight work finishes.
- Tap it to open the Tower at Budget.
- Why second: the product's original promise (stay awake, pause safely, don't run out of usage) is about deadlines, and a strip of time shows deadlines better than a card.

3. DECIDE (0-3 cards visible; '+N more' expands in place)
- Approval prompts, questions and plan approvals, ranked by reversibility class (Irreversible first, so it can't be buried), then by wait time.
- Card shape follows reversibility: Undoable is one compact line; Contained is two lines with the redacted command; Irreversible is tall with the full command.
- Every card carries its delivery preview line, for example 'Will type 1 · cmux › mac-on-claude-code · Studio MBP'.

4. LOOK (amber-edged)
- Things going wrong or about to: stuck (same failing command ×6 / no progress 15 min / stalled workflow), rate-limited ('resumes 03:05 · wake scheduled'), and forecasts that need a choice. Example: 'Cutoff in 22 min, 2 workflows still running · Pause gracefully now / Remind me to plug in'.

5. RETURN BRIEF (only after 45 min or more away)
- With nothing in Decide or Look, it is expanded directly under the Runway.
- Otherwise it sits here as one collapsed line: 'While you were away · 1h 52m ›'.

6. REVIEW
- Finished turns waiting for you, each with its what-changed headline: 'Changed 3 files (+120 −14) · tests passed'.

7. IN FLIGHT (a single horizontal ribbon of strands)
- One strand per working session or workflow: star glyph, project, last action in mono ('vitest · 212 passed'), elapsed time, and a 4-of-7 arc for workflows.
- Tap a strand to open the Session Room. Tap the section header to go to Sky.
- This answers 'what are they doing?' without leaving Now.

8. SETTLED
- Hairline receipts that fade with age: 'You approved swift test · 12m · iPhone · delivered'.
- Keep scrolling for earlier days, each collapsed to a headline card. This is where History went.

9. THE CAPSULE: Now · (pulse) · Sky.

ALL-QUIET STATE
- Sections 3-6 vanish and the Horizon grows to fill about 60% of the screen.
- The pulse breathes teal slowly, and the sentence reads 'All quiet · 5 agents working · runway clear till 06:00'.
- The Runway stays, because power always matters. The In-flight ribbon stays.
- The empty screen is the reward.

screens.name: 1. Now (the ranked stream)
screens.platform: iPhone (primary); Android same structure in M3 Expressive; Mac compact form in screen 8
screens.layout:
OVERALL ORDER
- Horizon (pulse 56 pt, dispatcher sentence in 17 pt semibold, Mac chip top-left), then Runway strip (44 pt), then the section headers DECIDE / LOOK / REVIEW in 11 pt uppercase caption with 0.8 tracking. Each header appears only when its section has items.
- Then the In-flight ribbon (horizontal, 72 pt), then the Settled hairlines, then the capsule.
- Glass cards are 16 pt from the edges with a 20 pt corner radius.

DECISION CARD ANATOMY
- Left: a 28 pt star glyph. Its colour comes from the project's constellation hue, and its shape is seeded from a hash of the cwd, so the same project always looks the same.
- Title: verb-first plain language from the prompt ('Run swift test', 'Edit 3 files in Sources/Relay', 'Approve plan: migrate relay to v2 · 7 steps', 'Question: which branch should I base this on?').
- Meta line: project · branch · Claude / Codex / Ollama · 'blocked 2:14'.
- Reversibility chip: Undoable / Contained / Irreversible, with the reason underneath in caption ('runs tests · inside repo · clean tree', or 'pushes to origin/main').
- Delivery preview line in 12 pt mono: 'Will type 1 · cmux › payments-api · Studio MBP'.

SHAPE BY CLASS
- Undoable: one line, 64 pt.
- Contained: two lines plus the redacted command, 104 pt.
- Irreversible: tall, with the full command in mono, dangerous tokens underlined, and the cwd. It has no swipe and shows only 'Review'.

OTHER CARDS
- Look cards: an amber left edge, plus a loop sparkline of the repeated tool call ('vitest failed ×6 in 9 min').
- Review cards: the diff headline, a test dot (teal for pass, amber for fail; never red), and the buttons 'Carry on' / 'Review'.
- Batch bar: when 3-5 Undoable decisions of the same kind stack up, a glass bar reads 'Clear the quick ones (3)'.
screens.interactions:
UNDOABLE CARDS
- Swipe right = Approve: the Mac types the prompt's option 1. Swipe left = Deny: the Mac presses Esc.
- The swipe commits at 40% of the card width, with a haptic at the threshold.

ALL CARDS
- Tap opens the Decision Sheet.
- Long-press: Hold (15 min / 1 h / until at desk), Open on Mac, Stop this session.
- The 'Tell it' bubble button opens an inline composer above the keyboard, labelled 'Esc, then your message', with standing-reply chips.

ORDERING SAFETY
- The order freezes while any card is touched, scrolled or expanded. New arrivals queue behind a 'New ↑ 1' glass pill at the top.
- A card is never re-sorted under a finger.

BATCH APPROVAL
- 'Clear the quick ones' opens a checklist of the exact items, all pre-checked and readable.
- One confirming tap sends each item individually, and each row resolves on its own delivery result.
- Batches contain Undoable items only, are capped at 5, and are never available from the lock screen.

REVIEW AND IN FLIGHT
- Review 'Carry on' sends your configured standing reply (default 'Carry on'). Review opens the Session Room on Changes.
- Tap an In-flight strand to open its Session Room.
- Swipe on the Horizon or the capsule to go to Sky.
screens.motion:
ARRIVAL ('final approach', signature 2)
- The card descends from the pulse with a faint contrail. Cards below ease down by exactly one card height (spring, response 0.45, damping 0.85). Nothing else moves.
- Under Reduce Motion it is a cross-fade.

SWIPE
- Swiping reveals a teal well (Approve) or a neutral slate well (Deny). Past 40% the session's star inside the well brightens.
- On release, the card runs the three-phase receipt (signature 3), holding its slot throughout:
  - ARM: a local 1.2 s ring. Nothing has been sent yet, and tapping the ring cancels.
  - SEND: the thread travels to the Mac chip. Cancel is no longer offered in this phase.
  - RESOLVE: the thread completes on a confirmed delivery, or snaps back with the outcome text.

OUTCOMES
- Delivered: the amber dot turns teal, its rings contract into the dot, and the card folds into a 1 pt hairline that drifts down into Settled.
- Not delivered: one soft shake, and the outcome in words.
- Deny slides the card left and dims it, never red.

THE PULSE
- When the last Decide card clears, the pulse moves from amber to teal over 800 ms with one long exhale, and the aurora settles.

screens.name: 2. Decision Sheet
screens.platform: iPhone and Android (bottom sheet ~88%); Mac shows the same content as an expanded popover row
screens.layout:
A glass sheet grows from the card's frame. The sky behind it blurs and darkens by 30%. Top to bottom:

1. IDENTITY
- Star glyph with the session's mini pulse, then project · branch · agent · 'blocked 3:02' · which Mac.

2. THE ASK
- In 22 pt mono, syntax-tinted, with risk tokens underlined. Example: 'git push --force-with-lease origin feat/relay-v2'.
- Below it: the cwd, and whether the git tree is clean or dirty.
- Edits show the hunk. Plans show numbered steps. Questions show the agent's options as large buttons.

3. WHY
- The agent's last assistant message before the prompt, 3 lines, expandable.

4. THIS TURN
- The TurnDigest tool calls as small ticks, with failures in amber.
- A live terminal thumbnail (tap to open Screen).

5. REVERSIBILITY PANEL
- The class and its reasons, plus 'what undo would look like': 'git reflog can recover this branch', or 'No undo: affects the remote'.

6. DELIVERY PREVIEW
- 'Will type 1 into cmux › relay pane on Studio MBP', or 'Will press Esc'.

7. ACTION BAR (pinned)
- The prompt's own options with their exact labels, except 'Yes, and don't ask again', which is never offered from the phone. Instead it reads 'Open in terminal to choose this'.
- Then 'Deny' (Esc), 'Tell it instead…' and 'Open Session Room'.
screens.interactions:
APPROVE, BY CLASS
- Undoable: tap, with the 1.2 s cancel ring.
- Contained: tap, with the 1.2 s cancel ring and the delivery preview highlighted.
- Irreversible: press and hold for 1.2 s, then Face ID / Touch ID / fingerprint. For these items the hold is the arm phase: Page sends as soon as biometrics succeed, with no second ring. It is never offered from the lock screen, a notification, a widget, Siri or a batch.

ANSWERING AND REDIRECTING
- Question options send the matching option number.
- 'Tell it instead…' unlocks the composer. Sending it delivers Esc, then the text, then Return.
- While the sheet is open, the composer field is locked. Free text can never be typed into a live prompt, because text plus Enter would approve it.

LIVE UPDATES AND DISMISSAL
- The sheet updates live. If the prompt is answered at the Mac, it shows 'Answered at the Mac · Approved' and closes itself after 1.5 s.
- If the prompt changed, it shows 'Prompt changed. Review again' with the new ask.
- Swipe down to dismiss without acting; the card returns to its slot unchanged.
- Swipe up for the next Decide item, so you can clear a queue without going back.
screens.motion:
OPENING
- A matched-geometry zoom out of the card.

THE HOLD BUTTON (signature 4)
- An amber ring fills clockwise around the thumb and warms to red only in its final third.
- Haptic ticks at 33%, 66% and 100%, then the biometric prompt.
- Letting go early unwinds the ring backwards, and nothing is sent.

AFTER APPROVAL
- The ask's mono text 'types itself' left to right, mirroring the keystroke delivered on the Mac.
- The receipt thread runs up to the Mac chip.
- The sheet resolves only on a confirmed result. On a failure it settles back with the outcome text in place of the action bar.

screens.name: 3. Sky (fleet: Sky mode and Lanes mode)
screens.platform: iPhone and Android full-screen; Android tablet two-pane; Mac compact strip in the popover
screens.interactions:
- Tap a star to show a glass tooltip: project, last action ('[Bash] swift test · 20 s ago') and Open.
- Double-tap a star, or tap Open, to fly into its Session Room.
- Pinch out on a constellation to focus a project. Pinch in to see the whole sky.
- Long-press a star or lane for Hold, Stop this session (hold 0.6 s, then Esc) and Open on Mac.
- In Lanes, pinch horizontally to change the time scale (1 h / 4 h / day).
- Tap the moon to open the Tower at Power.
- Swipe the Horizon or the capsule to go back to Now.
- Amber stars always also exist as cards in Now. Nothing actionable lives only in Sky.
screens.motion:
NOW TO SKY
- The aurora pans right as one sky. Every card's star glyph flies to its star (shared element), so you see that cards and stars are the same sessions.

STARS
- Each real tool call makes its star twinkle once. A stalled star stops twinkling, and that stillness is the signal.
- Aurora intensity and drift follow total activity, and go nearly still when all is idle.
- A session that ends cools to an ember over 3 s.
- A dispatched session is born as a flare at its constellation.
- During a battery pause, the sky plays dusk (signature 5).

SKY AND LANES
- Switching modes morphs each star into its lane's 'now' node, and each constellation unrolls into its group.

screens.name: 4. Session Room (with Review mode)
screens.platform: iPhone and Android full-screen push; Android tablet detail pane; Mac opens the real terminal instead (O key) or a small Changes panel
screens.interactions:
- Swipe between lenses, except in Screen, where horizontal pans scroll wide output and the segment bar switches lenses.
- Stop is a 0.6 s hold, because Esc interrupts the turn.
- In Screen, pinch to zoom, double-tap to fit the width, and swipe up with two fingers for scrollback. While a permission prompt is on screen, free typing hides and only the safe actions show.
- In Changes, long-press a file or tap a hunk to quote it into the composer ('Why did you change this?'). 'Ask for changes' prefills the composer with the file context.
- Quick replies such as 'Commit this', 'Open a PR' and 'Write tests for this' are sent as instructions to the agent. Page never runs git itself.
- 'Open on Mac' brings the real terminal window or cmux pane forward.
- Back: edge swipe on iOS, predictive back on Android.
screens.motion:
OPENING AND CLOSING
- The room zooms from its origin (card, star, lane or strand). Back shrinks it into the same spot.

STORY AND SCREEN
- New transcript lines rise gently.
- A faint teal 'thinking' shimmer runs along the composer edge while busy, at a speed matched to the output rate.
- On Screen, only changed rows cross-fade, and a scanline passes per frame received. If frames stop for 30 s while the session is busy, the live dot slows and turns amber.

CHANGES AND WORKFLOWS
- The evidence chips count up once.
- Workflow nodes fill teal one by one, and the ring closes with one soft pulse when every agent is done.

screens.name: 5. Return Brief (the handover moment)
screens.platform: iPhone and Android at the top of Now; Mac as the Welcome back panel
screens.layout:
WHEN IT APPEARS
- After 45 min or more away, judged by the phone's last open plus Mac UserPresence.
- It sits at the top of Now, or below Decide and Look when either has items (rule zero).

THE CARD
- A tall glass card titled 'While you were away · 1h 52m · 23:20 to 01:12'.
- Three large counts in display type: Finished 3 · In flight 2 · Need you 2. Under each, 1-2 lines naming the items.
- Rows:
  - 'Decided: 9 (8 approved, 1 denied) · 6 from iPhone, 3 at the Mac';
  - 'Finished: 3 turns · 11 files · tests passing in 2 of 3';
  - 'Stuck and recovered: 1';
  - 'Usage: 5h 38% → 71% · on pace to hit 03:10, resets 03:40';
  - 'Battery: 64% → 41% · awake, lid closed · paused at cutoff 0 times'.
- Footer actions: 'Review the 3 finished' and 'Dismiss'.

DATA
- Everything comes deterministically from Page's own page/reply/delivery log, TurnSummary headlines, and the usage and battery readings Page already takes. No model call is needed.
screens.interactions:
- Tap a row to expand its items. Each item links to its card or Session Room.
- 'Review the finished' scrolls to and highlights the Review cards.
- Tap a count to settle into Now with that section focused.
- Swipe the Brief away to dismiss it. Pull down past the Horizon detent to bring it back.
- On the Mac, the panel shows for 8 s when presence returns, and clicking it opens the popover. If you cleared everything from the phone, it reads 'You handled 6 from iPhone'.
screens.motion:
- A short sunrise: the aurora brightens from the horizon in proportion to how much finished while you were away. A big, productive absence is a bright dawn; an idle one stays dim.
- The Brief unfurls downward from the Horizon, and the numbers count up in under 400 ms.
- On settle, each count flies to its section (Need you to Decide, Finished to Review, In flight to the ribbon), so you learn where things live by watching them go there.
- Dismissing folds the Brief into one Settled hairline: 'Brief · 1h 52m away'.
- If any Decide card exists, the sunrise is skipped entirely.
- Under Reduce Motion it is a cross-fade with static counts.

screens.name: 6. Dispatch (start new work)
screens.platform: iPhone and Android sheet from the pulse / FAB; Mac panel via Command-N or Option-Command-P then N
screens.layout:
A glass sheet rising from the pulse. Top to bottom:

1. PROJECT
- Chips of known project folders, most recent first. Each shows its star glyph and its last outcome ('tests passed · 2 h ago'), with a search field.

2. AGENT
- Claude / Codex / local model. Only agents present on the live Mac are shown.

3. PROMPT
- A large field with dictation and saved templates.

4. 'PAGE ME FOR'
- Decisions only / Decisions and finished / Everything. This sets the session's attention level.

5. WHEN
- 'Start now' is the primary action and is shipped behaviour.
- 'When the 5h window resets 03:40', 'When the Mac is on power' and 'When I step away' appear only once the Mac-side start queue ships (v4.3). Queued items show underneath as dim seeds with their trigger.

6. A SHRUNK RUNWAY
- So you see the battery and usage you are spending into. An amber marker shows when the cutoff or the limit will land before a typical turn ends.

7. 'START ON STUDIO MBP'
- Always names the Mac.
screens.interactions:
- 'Start now' sends the request to SessionStarter.
- If no session appears within 90 s, or the Mac refuses, the sheet says plainly where to look (existing behaviour).
- On Android, the FAB's container transform opens the sheet.
- 'Continue this thread' from any Review card or Session Room prefills the same session, instead of starting a new one.
- Swipe a queued seed to delete it.
- A press on the pulse shorter than 300 ms counts as a tap and opens Dispatch. Anything longer starts the Stop ring. Voice-first Dispatch therefore lives on a mic button inside the sheet, which focuses dictation the moment the sheet opens. The pulse never carries a third gesture.
screens.motion:
- On Start, the sheet collapses into a spark that arcs from the pulse to Sky's capsule icon, which glints once.
- The new star flares in its constellation only when the Mac confirms the session exists.

screens.name: 7. The Tower (power, budget, Macs, settings)
screens.platform: iPhone and Android sheet from the Mac chip or Runway; Mac Preferences window
screens.layout:
A sheet drops from the Mac chip. Sections, top to bottom:

1. POWER (hero)
- A battery ring with the cutoff marked as a draggable notch, and a forecast arc: 'At current drain the agents pause at 15% in 1h 52m'.
- Status: 'Awake · lid closed · on battery'.
- Toggles: keep-awake mode; lid-closed on AC (default on); the lid-closed-on-battery opt-in, with its watchdog note; 'Pause agents gracefully at cutoff' (on).
- A log of pauses and resumes: 'Paused 3 at 15% · 02:14 · resumed on power 07:40'.

2. BUDGET
- Concentric 5h and 7d rings with reset times, a pace tick against an even burn, and 'On pace to hit the 5h limit at 03:10, resets 03:40'.
- A 24 h burn chart with finished turns plotted as points.
- A per-project breakdown, labelled 'needs per-session accounting' until it ships.

3. MACS
- The paired Macs, with the live one marked and the others shown as standby. Tap one to make it live.

4. ATTENTION
- Modes: At desk (blocking only), Away (everything), Asleep (blocking plus battery cutoff; the rest goes into the morning Brief).
- Quiet hours, the 'away' threshold, and per-project attention levels.

5. STANDING REPLIES
- Your saved instructions, editable. These are the only words Page ever sends on your behalf.

6. AGENT HOOKS
- An install/status card that shows the diff before writing ~/.claude or ~/.codex settings, with backup and opt-in.

7. PAIRING AND ENCRYPTION

8. STOP MY AGENTS
- A hold-to-confirm button at the foot.
screens.interactions:
- Drag the cutoff notch: a haptic detent every 5%, and the forecast arc and the Runway's battery marker update live.
- Tapping the Runway opens the Tower scrolled to Budget. Tapping the moon in Sky opens it at Power.
- Tap a usage ring to flip it to the burn chart.
- Switching the live Mac re-keys the app: the stream reloads and the sky re-forms.
- Settings live next to the consequence they control.
screens.motion:
- The sheet drops from the chip. The battery ring drains in real time.
- When the cutoff is near, the notch glows amber and the aurora behind the sheet warms.
- The Attention mode selector moves the pulse between three intensities: dim (desk), full (away), slow and low (asleep).
- Switching Macs disperses the stars and re-forms them into the new Mac's constellations (~1 s).
- The rings fill from 0 on open, and the pace tick sways slightly ahead of or behind the even-burn line.

A liquid-glass popover, 380 pt wide. Top to bottom:

1. HORIZON LINE

2. RUNWAY

WELCOME BACK PANEL

KEYBOARD
- Up/Down, 1, Esc, T, O, Command-N, hold Command-period.

THE GLYPH
- Teal breath; amber ripple with a count; a hollow ring when keep-awake is off; a moon tick for lid-closed; a battery-headroom hairline arc.

WHEN YOU WALK AWAY

trustModel:
PRINCIPLE: Page never decides for you. It makes your own decision fast where speed is safe and slower where it isn't, and it shows a receipt for every keystroke. There is no auto-allow and no auto-deny anywhere, which matches the roadmap rule.

1. KEYSTROKE TRUTH (enforced in the Mac reply planner, not only in the UI)
- Approve types the prompt's option 1. Deny presses Esc.
- Any written reply to an open prompt is sent as Esc, then the text, then Return. Text plus Enter on a Claude prompt approves the highlighted 'Yes', so the composer is locked while a session is waiting, and the Mac refuses free text into a waiting prompt that doesn't start with Esc.
- Page never sends '2'. 'Yes, and don't ask again' is never offered from the phone, watch, widget or Siri. It reads 'Open in terminal to choose this'.
- Steer while busy sends text plus Enter, which queues. Stop while busy sends Esc, which interrupts, behind a 0.6 s hold.
- Codex and local models get their own adapters. There is no assumed parity, and an unknown agent prompt shows 'Couldn't tell what's on screen · Open on Mac'.

2. DELIVERY PREVIEW
- Every action states what will be typed and where: 'Will type 1 · cmux › payments-api · Studio MBP' / 'Will press Esc' / 'Esc, then your message'.
- Actions always name the Mac, so with several Macs paired you can't act on the wrong one.

3. STILL-LIVE CHECK BEFORE EVERY INJECTION
The Mac re-checks three things:
- the pid is alive (stale session files after crashes are ignored);
- the status is still 'waiting';
- the on-screen prompt matches the fingerprint the phone showed (the existing input-gate staleness check, extended with a screen hash).
If any check fails, nothing is typed, and the card shows 'Already answered at the Mac' or 'Prompt changed · Review again'.

4. REVERSIBILITY CLASSES (new: a conservative classifier on the Mac)
- Inputs: the tool kind (edit / command / plan); Bash patterns (read-only, test and build vs rm, force-push, deploy, migrations, sudo, curl|sh, writes); whether the target is inside the cwd; git repo plus clean tree; remote or branch effects.
- It sends only the class plus short reason tags to the phone. The tags are Read-only, Edits in repo, Runs commands, Network/outside repo and Destructive. Unknown always means Contained or worse.
- UNDOABLE: swipe; batchable (max 5, same kind); notification actions available, but only after unlock.
- CONTAINED: tap in the app with a 1.2 s cancel ring. Notifications offer only 'Open to decide'.
- IRREVERSIBLE: full command shown, press and hold 1.2 s plus biometrics. Never from the lock screen, a notification, a widget, Siri or a batch. On the Mac it needs Touch ID, or the login password where there is no Touch ID.
- Chips are hints, never a 'safe' badge. There is no green 'safe' state.
- Misclassification signal: an Undoable approval followed within 2 min by the user stopping that session is logged for review.

5. DELIVERY TRUTH: animations wait for results
- Success plays only on a confirmed 'delivered'. Every other outcome has its own words and a next step:
  - timed out → 'Didn't confirm in time · Check on Mac';
  - session gone → 'Session ended';
  - not typable → 'This terminal can't take input · Open on Mac';
  - busy → 'Queued after this turn';
  - digit while busy → 'Prompt closed before your answer';
  - answered live → 'Already answered at the Mac';
  - unknown state → 'Review again'.
- Page never retries an approval automatically.
- Every action runs Arm, then Send, then Resolve.
  - ARM is a local 1.2 s ring during which nothing has left the phone and Cancel works. For Irreversible items, the hold plus biometrics is the arm.
  - Once SEND begins, there is no cancel, because keystrokes can't be taken back. The UI never offers an undo it can't honour.

6. DELEGATION IS ALWAYS YOUR WORDS OR YOUR TAPS
- Standing replies you wrote.
- Per-session attention levels and Hold.
- Batch review where every item is visible and is sent individually.
- Queued 'when done, tell it…' instructions (v4.1).
- Standing instructions, never standing permissions. Any rule that would change an agent's own permission config is a separate, user-decided feature (see Beyond).

7. STOP IS ALWAYS ONE GESTURE AWAY
- Hold the pulse, or hold Command-period: a 300 ms dead zone, a 1.5 s fill, biometrics, then the scope is named ('Press Esc in 4 busy sessions').
- Results come back per session, and the stars or lanes go still as each receipt arrives.

8. PRIVACY
- The relay, APNs and FCM carry only counts, the project name, the kind and the already-redacted one-liner.
- Commands, file names, diffs and transcripts load end-to-end encrypted after unlock.
- Session Rooms can require biometrics after 5 min away.
- Any future LLM-written summary runs on the Mac, never on the relay.

9. AUDIT IN PLACE
- Every human action becomes a Settled receipt and a Story line: 'You approved npm test · 14:02 · iPhone · delivered'.
- The full audit log sits in the Tower.

10. CALM, NOT ALARMING
- Amber means 'needs you'. Deny is neutral slate. Failed tests are amber.
- Red appears in exactly two places: the final third of the Irreversible hold ring, and the Stop-all ring.
- Pulse urgency rises gently with wait time and is capped.
- Finished turns never page while you're at the desk. Forecasts page only when they will land before in-flight work ends. Every Look item has a Hold. Stuck, rate-limit and battery-cutoff pages break through Asleep mode.
signatureAnimations:
1. THE PULSE (heartbeat of the whole product). One glyph on every surface: the Horizon, the capsule, the menu bar, the Live Activity, widgets and the Quick Settings tile.
- Teal breath at 4 s, slightly faster with more agents working.
- Amber ripple, one ring per waiting item; the rate rises with the longest wait, capped at one every 1.5 s.
- Still star-white when quiet.
- When the last Decide item clears: amber to teal over 800 ms with one long exhale, and the aurora settles.
- Reduce Motion: a static ring with a count.

2. FINAL APPROACH (arrival). A new decision descends from the pulse into its ranked slot, trailing a faint contrail.
- Only cards below the slot ease down, by exactly one card height. Nothing above moves, and nothing re-sorts under a finger.
- If you are touching or scrolling, it waits behind a 'New ↑ 1' pill.
- The same motion plays in the Mac popover and the Live Activity (one ripple).

3. THE RECEIPT THREAD (delivery truth made visible). It plays in three phases, the same on every surface.
- ARM (0-1.2 s): a local ring winds around the card's dot. Nothing has been sent, and a tap cancels. For Irreversible items, the press-and-hold plus biometrics is the arm phase.
- SEND: a thin thread of light leaves the card and travels up to the Mac chip. It can no longer be cancelled, and nothing on screen says otherwise.
- RESOLVE: the thread completes only when the Mac confirms the keystroke landed. Then the card's amber dot turns teal, its rings contract into the dot, and the card folds into a hairline that drifts into Settled.
- If delivery fails or the prompt changed, the thread snaps back, the card shakes once softly, and the outcome appears in words.

4. THE HOLD RING (deliberate commitment). Used only for Irreversible approvals and Stop-all.
- A ring fills clockwise around the thumb: amber, warming to red only in its final third.
- Haptic ticks at 33%, 66% and 100%, then the biometric prompt.
- Releasing early unwinds the ring backwards and nothing is sent.
- For Stop-all, each session's star or lane goes still as its Esc receipt arrives.

5. DUSK AND DAWN (power, the original promise).
- When Page pauses agents at the battery cutoff, the aurora fades to dusk, every working star exhales and dims together, and a grey horizon band crosses the affected lanes. The menu-bar glyph settles to a low glow: 'Paused for battery · resumes on power'.
- When power returns, a dawn sweep rises from the horizon and relights each star one by one, as each session's resume is confirmed.
- The same sunrise, scaled to how much finished, opens the Return Brief after an absence.
beyond: v4.0, ships with the redesign (new work, on existing data): the Mac-side reversibility classifier; the Live Activity / Dynamic Island and the Android 16 live-update notification (both new surfaces; widgets and Siri exist today); the Return Brief aggregator over the page/reply/delivery log; the Mac Welcome back panel and Step away; the screen-fingerprint extension to the input gate; a per-session state-transition log on the Mac (feeds Lanes strips, the Brief and wait-cost); star glyphs seeded from a hash of the cwd (no registry).

v4.1, Review and steering: a per-file 'Looks good / Ask about this' review lane over the existing encrypted diff kind; loop remedies as standing replies ('Stop and explain what's failing', 'Try a different approach'); queued 'When done, tell it…' handoffs, where the Mac types your text when the status turns idle (only needs a small queue plus existing status observation and injection); a Morning Brief in Asleep mode ('what ran overnight, what's waiting, today's runway'); and earlier same-folder Claude sessions in the Session Room's Story (new relay request).

v4.2, Outcome ledger and cost: the Mac reads git log (and optionally gh pr list/view) in each session's repo since the turn started, so outcomes advance from Finished to Committed, Pushed and PR opened, and committed work keeps its evidence (TurnSummary diffs against HEAD go empty today). Per-session token accounting summed from transcript usage fields, which TranscriptParser already reads, gives '% of the 5h window this turn burned', Sky star brightness by burn, and the per-project Budget breakdown. Codex needs its own usage reader. Ollama shows compute time and battery drain, never dollars unless an API-billed account makes them real.

v4.3, Runway-aware dispatch: 'Start when the 5h window resets', 'When the Mac is on power' and 'When I step away', as a Mac-side queue of pending starts extending ResumeScheduler and its pmset wake, each shown as a seed on the Runway. Plus a before-you-go check that compares BatteryForecast with workflow progress.

WAIT COST, shown gently: 'agent-minutes spent waiting on you today: 34', with the slowest hours highlighted, to help choose Carry-on defaults and when to step away. It is insight, never a streak or a guilt metric.

STANDUP AND WEEKLY CARD: day and week headline cards in Settled export as text (finished per project, PRs once v4.2 exists, tests, usage share). They are written deterministically, and optionally polished by a headless Claude run on the Mac.

SUGGEST A RULE, gated on your decision because it shifts trust. After you approve the same Undoable command 20 or more times in one repo, Page offers to add it to Claude's own allowlist in that project's .claude/settings.local.json (never the checked-in settings.json), via the existing hook installer: show the exact rule, back up, merge idempotently, list it in the Tower with delete. Claude only until there is a Codex mapping. The agent stops asking because you changed its config, not because Page approved for you.

PAGE TERMINAL INTEGRATION: replies go straight into the PTY with exact prompt detection. The 'not typable' and 'unknown state' outcomes mostly disappear, the still-live check becomes exact, and decision cards render inline in an amber pane gutter using the same component as the popover.
WRIST: the pulse as an Apple Watch complication and a Wear OS tile. Undoable approvals by double-tap after wrist unlock. Contained and above show 'Open on phone'.

FLEET ACROSS MACS: several Macs' constellations in one sky and their lanes in one Lanes list. It needs concurrent end-to-end channels in the relay and protocol, plus a Mac dimension on every card. Until then, standby Macs are clearly dimmed and Page never shows cross-Mac totals.
TEAM ON-CALL (later): hand a project's pages to a teammate during your quiet hours. It needs multi-user relay accounts and per-project sharing keys, which is a substantial new trust model.
macMenuBar:
ROLE: the Mac is where the work happens and where Page holds authority. It watches the sessions, delivers the keystrokes, and controls power. The menu bar is ambient by default and becomes the dispatcher whenever you are at the desk.

GLYPH: the pulse itself.
- Teal breath while agents work.
- Amber ripple with a small count when something is blocked.
- A hollow ring when keep-awake is off.
- A moon tick when lid-closed awake is active.
- A hairline arc around the dot showing battery headroom to the cutoff.
- A flat horizon line under a dimmed dot while agents are paused for battery.
- A small phone badge when phone paging is armed because you're away.

POPOVER: click the glyph, or press Option-Command-P from anywhere. It is 380 pt of liquid glass, compact Now:
- the Horizon line;
- the Runway (battery cutoff, 5h limit, resets, scheduled resumes);
- Decide, Look and Review rows, each with a reversibility chip and delivery preview;
- the In-flight strip with workflow arcs;
- a 'Now | Sky' segment (a compact constellation band plus Lanes);
- the footer: Step away, Stop my agents (hold), Preferences.

KEYBOARD
- Up/Down to move.
- 1 approves. Return approves Undoable items only.
- Esc denies. T means 'Tell it instead' (Esc first). O focuses the exact Terminal, iTerm2 or cmux pane.
- Command-N opens Dispatch. Holding Command-period stops all agents.
- Irreversible items default to O; approving one in place requires Touch ID (or the login password on Macs without Touch ID).

PRESENCE HAND-OFF (UserPresence)
- At the desk: finished, idle and forecast pages stay on the Mac and the phone stays quiet. Approvals and questions page both devices, resolve on whichever answers first, and the other shows 'Answered on Mac' / 'Answered on iPhone'.
- Going idle past the away threshold, or pressing Step away, sends one outward ripple, arms the phone, starts the Live Activity, keeps the Mac awake with the lid closed (on AC by default, on battery only with the opt-in and watchdog), and runs the before-you-go battery check.
- On return, the Welcome back panel drops for 8 s with the handover, amber first, or 'You handled 6 from iPhone'.

POWER IN THE SAME LANGUAGE
- The cutoff is a Runway marker.
- At the cutoff, Page asks every busy agent to pause at a safe point, pages the phone once, and plays dusk.
- On power it resumes them and plays dawn.

PREFERENCES
- The full Tower: hooks installer with diff and backup, cmux bridge, power helper, cutoff, lid behaviour, pairing, and the audit log. These are never terminal steps.
